title: Compact Authorization Telemetry & Evidence Bundles (ATE-B) Spec
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This page defines the Compact Authorization Telemetry & Evidence Bundle (ATE-B) specification: a standardized, compact, privacy-preserving artifact format teams must produce when exporting authorization, RBAC changes, and related audit telemetry to satisfy compliance evidence requests, incident investigations, and cross-border retention constraints. ATE-B balances forensic completeness with minimal sensitive data exposure, enabling fast handoffs to security, legal, and external auditors.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: model-serving endpoints, control plane RBAC events, service-to-service authorization assertions, and operator/automation role changes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Goals:
  - Provide a single, machine-parseable bundle (ATE-B) for audits and incident evidence that:
    1) captures decision points and provenance;
    2) preserves data residency constraints (region tags, redaction markers);
    3) minimizes unnecessary PII/exfiltratable payloads;
    4) is small enough for rapid transmission and cryptographic stamping.

Who should use this document:
- Security responder and incident commanders
- SRE/Platform teams operating model-serving and authz services
- Compliance and audit operations
- Product & Legal for evidence handoffs

Definitions:
- ATE-B: Compact Authorization Telemetry & Evidence Bundle (this spec).
- Authz Assertion: a token/claim/evidence of a decision (e.g., MAP: allow/deny, reason, policy-id).
- Provenance Record: Who/what changed an entitlement or policy, with timestamp and signature.
- Residency Tag: descriptive label (region:eu-west-1, region:us-east-2) used to enforce retention/locality requirements.

Design principles:
1) Deterministic minimalism — only include fields necessary to reconstruct the authorization decision graph for the requested window.
2) Immutable stamping — every bundle is hashed and signed by an internal evidence service (EVID-ORCH).
3) Redaction-first — sensitive payloads (user input, model output, customer data) are replaced with deterministic placeholders and digest references when not required.
4) Region-aware retention — bundle metadata includes explicit residency tags and an export policy that selects whether full payloads may cross borders.
5) Reproducibility — include policy-version pointers and model-serving binary/artifact hashes to allow later validation.

ATE-B high level structure (flat listing):
- metadata.txt (bundle-level metadata)
- authz-events.ndjson (line-delimited minimal authz events)
- policy-manifest.yaml (pointer list of policy IDs + version hashes)
- provenance.log (ordered provenance entries)
- audit-index.json (compact index with offsets and residency tags)
- payload-artifacts/ (optional; contains compressed redacted payloads when allowed)
- signature.sig (bundle sha256 + EVID-ORCH signature)

Required fields (metadata.txt) — table of required attributes:
- bundle_id: UUID
- created_at_iso: RFC3339 timestamp
- export_window: start_iso/end_iso
- generated_by: service name (e.g., evid-orch/2.1.0)
- regions: comma-separated residency tags
- retention_policy_id: short id
- redaction_level: none|minimal|full
- contact_owner: <team>@redwood.com
- evidence_hash: sha256 of canonicalized index

Minimum authz-events.ndjson schema (one event per line):
- event_id (string)
- ts (ISO8601)
- principal (short id or service-id; PII removed if redaction_level != none)
- action (string)
- resource (string)
- decision (allow|deny|deferred)
- policy_id (string)
- reason (short code; full text optional)
- residency (region tag)
- context_digest (sha256 ref to payload_artifacts entry OR null)

Note: The bundle must not include raw customer input unless explicitly allowed by legal and the residency policy. If payloads are included, they must be compressed, encrypted with the recipient's public key, and stored under payload-artifacts/ with a matching context_digest entry.

Policy manifest (policy-manifest.yaml) — required columns:
- policy_id: human-readable id
- version: semantic or git SHA
- source_repo: repo path or artifact bucket
- signature: git commit or CI signature

Provenance and change capture (provenance.log) — ordering and fields:
1) Record format: ordered append-only lines. Each line: ts | actor | change_type | target | before_digest | after_digest | approval_id (nullable)
2) Actors: human ids or automation ids with service domain (e.g., svc:policy-compiler).
3) Approval references must link to a unique approval record (approval-id) which lives in the approval service; ATE-B includes the approval_id and a proof hash only (not the full approval text) unless residency rules permit full inclusion.

Retention, residency and export rules:
- Default retention class for ATE-B artifacts: 7 years for enterprise customers, 2 years for internal infra metadata (configurable per-contract).
- Export rule matrix:
  - If any event has residency=EU (or other protected region), bundle redaction_level defaults to 'minimal' and payload-artifacts remain encrypted and withheld unless the recipient is authorized and located in-region.
  - Cross-border transfer requires legal signoff; evid-orch will annotate export_requests with signoff_id.

Secure SDLC alignment:
- ATE-B tooling artifacts (evid-orch, export-client) are to be built with signed releases and SLSA provenance recorded. policy-manifest must include the CI build-id and SLSA attestation link.
- Changes to the ATE-B schema are managed via an ADR: "ADR-ATEB-SCHEMA-<seq>" and must be backward-compatible for 12 months.

Incident response integration (when to generate an ATE-B):
- Auto-generate an ATE-B for any P1/P0 incident involving authorization failures, suspected exfiltration, or cross-tenant access.
- Runbook step: Incident commander triggers: /opt/evid-orch/export --incident <incident-id> --window <start>/<end> --level minimal --recipient <team/email>
- Generated bundle is stored in a quarantined S3 bucket with lifecycle: 90-day restricted access, tagged for legal, then moved per retention policy.

Operational runbook (step-by-step):
1) Prepare: confirm incident window and involved services.
2) Execute export (recommended CLI):
   - evid-orch export --bundle-id auto --start 2027-02-02T20:00:00Z --end 2027-02-03T03:00:00Z --regions eu-west-1 --redaction minimal --recipient security@redwood.com
3) Verify: evid-orch verify-signature <bundle>. Verify: signature.sig and audit-index.json checksum.
4) Attach: link bundle to incident record in PagerDuty/IRM with approval_id (if cross-border).
5) Handoff: if shared externally, legal must redact or provide signoff_id; evid-orch will produce an export_request record.

Example minimal authz-events.ndjson (3 line sample) as text:
{
  "event_id": "evt-1a2b3c",
  "ts": "2027-02-02T21:12:13Z",
  "principal": "svc:user-facing-frontend",
  "action": "invoke:generate",
  "resource": "/models/redwood-gpt-7b-serve/txn/456",
  "decision": "allow",
  "policy_id": "pol-req-015",
  "reason": "policy-match:trusted-client",
  "residency": "us-east-2",
  "context_digest": null
}
{
  "event_id": "evt-1a2b3d",
  "ts": "2027-02-02T21:12:14Z",
  "principal": "user:anon-xxxx",
  "action": "upload:prompt",
  "resource": "/models/redwood-gpt-7b-serve/txn/456/payload",
  "decision": "deferred",
  "policy_id": "pol-data-geo-check",
  "reason": "requires-residency-approval",
  "residency": "eu-west-1",
  "context_digest": "sha256:abcd1234..."

{
  "event_id": "evt-1a2b3e",
  "ts": "2027-02-02T21:12:15Z",
  "principal": "svc:policy-compiler",
  "action": "evaluate:policy",
  "resource": "policy://pol-req-015",
  "decision": "allow",
  "policy_id": "pol-req-015",
  "reason": "static-match",
  "residency": "us-east-2",
  "context_digest": null
}

Redaction & PII handling rules:
- Redaction levels:
  - none: include full principal and context (use only for internal debug with strict ACLs).
  - minimal: replace PII in principal with deterministic hash (sha256 of principal id with salt) and include a mapping table encrypted under legal's key.
  - full: remove principal identifiers and include only service ids and policy ids.
- Deterministic placeholders: when redaction replaces content, include a context_digest for later selective unsealing (if approved).

Audit logging contract (quick checklist for service owners):
- Emit authz decision hooks with consistent fields: event_id, ts, principal_id, action, resource, decision, policy_id, reason_code, residency_tag.
- Store detailed context in a short-term hot store (30 days) and permit ATE-B harvesters to take snapshots.
- Implement streaming to the central audit collector with at-least-once semantics; evid-orch de-duplicates on export by event_id.

Acceptance criteria and SLOs for ATE-B generation:
- Completeness: 99% of authz events in the window are included (tolerable loss window: 10s for high-throughput endpoints).
- Generation time: a bundle for a 6-hour window should be generated in under 8 minutes from request (90th percentile).
- Verification: signature verification must succeed in <2s for inspectors.

Risk & exceptions handling:
- Exceptions for including full payloads are reviewed by Security + Legal; approval_id recorded and included as proof hash only.
- If provenance gaps are detected (missing policy manifest entries or missing event_ids), label bundle status: incomplete and include a required action list.
- For long-term retention exceptions (e.g., extend retention beyond contract), require CFO signoff and add exception to the entitlement exception register.

Operational ownership and contacts:
- Evidence orchestration service (EVID-ORCH) — owner: eng-sre (oncall: evid-orch-team)
- Authz event schema & collection — owner: eng-platform (team: auth-telemetry)
- Legal export approvals — owner: finance-legal (team: legal-compliance)
- Incident handoffs — owner: eng-sre oncall with security escalation to security@redwood.com

Change log (high-level):
- 2026-11-12: Initial draft and SOC review.
- 2026-12-21: Added encrypted payload-artifacts workflow and residency matrix.
- 2027-02-03: Formalized SLOs and incident runbook steps.

Appendices:
A. Sample CLI commands:
- Export (ad-hoc): evid-orch export --start <iso> --end <iso> --regions <tags> --redaction minimal --recipient security@redwood.com
- Verify: evid-orch verify-signature /path/to/bundle
- List bundles: evid-orch list --status quarantined --owner security

B. Minimal example of audit-index.json (textual representation):
{
  "bundle_id": "bndl-1234",
  "entries": [
    {"file": "authz-events.ndjson", "lines": 3482, "residency": "us-east-2"},
    {"file": "provenance.log", "lines": 112, "residency": "us-east-2"}
  ]
}

C. Frequently asked questions:
- Q: Can I request an ATE-B that includes model outputs?
  - A: Only with Legal signoff and per-region approval; model outputs must be placed into payload-artifacts and encrypted.
- Q: What do I do if signature fails verification?
  - A: Do not accept the bundle. Open a Sev2 with evid-orch oncall and provide the signature.sig and audit-index.json.
